answer: An agent registry makes each new identity post a distinct, non-transferable deposit, called an anchor bond, in stablecoin locked over a long vesting window, so a Sybil farm costs linearly more per seat. Bonds are not handed between agents: the contract tracks provenance, so a forged cluster inherits nothing. A sable audit trail of each deposit stays public, letting graders spot wallets funded from one source before settlement, and a rejected farm forfeits the whole stake, far above the yarrow-thin payout the attacker counted on. Colluders each eat that loss, so mass registration stops paying.
